title: Pack a shock-sensitive sensor box with one of four identical-looking foam pads
instruction: Pack the blue-tagged sensor box A for the drop test. Put it flat on the foam in one of the four cartons, close the lid and push the closed lid down with at least 5 N to tuck its flap, then release it. About 2 seconds after the tucked carton and its contents are untouched, the tester lifts it 30 cm, holds it briefly and releases it onto the table. Keep both hands and any held object away throughout the test and for 2 seconds after landing. Finish with A flat on the pad in the closed, tucked carton, all cartons and boxes untouched and A still within 2 mm for the final 1 second. Do not exceed either box's 50 g shock rating or the stated force limits.
context: Protective packaging requires choosing suitable cushioning as well as closing a package. Pads that look alike can have different compliance; a package that appears intact can expose its contents to a damaging drop shock.
setup: One fixed layout; world coordinates in metres, +Z up. The station table top is at z = 0.7475. Four free rectangular cartons with 170 x 130 x 82 mm interiors and 4 mm rigid walls and floor have floor-top origins at (0.32, -0.22, 0.7515), (0.55, -0.22, 0.7515), (0.32, 0.10, 0.7515) and (0.55, 0.10, 0.7515), numbered by black marks. Each holds an unmarked foam insert, nominally 170 x 130 x 30 mm and 30 g, with an effective top support of 164 x 124 mm, and has a 40 g hinged lid that starts open at 1.75 rad. Each empty assembly weighs 270 g: a 200 g rigid carton base, the 40 g lid and the 30 g foam (15 g fixed in the base, 15 g in the moving top face). Two gray 120 x 68 x 50 mm sensor boxes start between the carton rows: blue-tagged A at (0.29, -0.06, 0.7725), 247.1 g, and green-tagged B at (0.45, -0.06, 0.7725), 628.9 g. Both have shock indicators that start white. Robot: bimanual YAM on the standard station, arm bases at (0, +/-0.305, 0.75), starting in the ready pose with grippers open; joint torque limits are 27 N m on the first three arm joints and 7 N m on the last three, and fingers are limited to 40 N. One overhead and two wrist RGB cameras; standard station floor, table and camera mount. Exact primitive geometry and poses are in setup-inventory.json, runtime/fixture.json and runtime/assets/.
scoring: Pass/fail (0 or 1): a drop test either protects the sensor or it does not, so there is no partial credit. Score 1 requires a completed physical drop of the tucked carton holding A, with no robot contact: lifted at least 0.25 m, released, and observed for at least 2 s after landing, with A's peak shock (2 ms proper acceleration) strictly below 50 g. Two independent recorders log each drop; they must agree on the boxes inside, on robot contact and on peak shock (within 3 g or 15%). At the end A must be in that same dropped carton: its centre over the 170 x 130 mm pad footprint, its lower face above the carton floor and at most 35 mm above it, tilted at most 10 degrees relative to the carton; the lid closed to at most 0.012 rad and tucked; the carton upright within 5 degrees and within 4 mm of its rest height. For the last 1 s the robot must touch no carton or box and A must stay within 2 mm. Score 0 if either box ever exceeds 50 g, the foam simulation diverges, the robot touches the package while the tester lifts, holds or drops it or in the 2 s after landing, or either arm's wrist force or force on a package stays above 80 N for 100 ms. Missing or unverified measurements score 0, and so does exceeding 1,604 steps (80.2 s).
reset_notes: Restore the fixed layout: both arms in the ready pose with grippers open, both indicators white, all four lids open at 1.75 rad and untucked, and the automatic testers armed. Clear all shock, contact, force, drop and final-hold history. No object pose randomization.
fidelity: Rigid cartons, lids and boxes; no cardboard tearing or flap flex. Each foam pad is a passive rigid top face (6 degrees of freedom) with global compression, tilt and shear compliance, damping and densification; no corner warping or foam side collisions. The tuck is a hinge constraint gated by lid contact and push force. The tester lifts with a finite 25 N / 2 N m drive, then releases into free fall. Shock is time-weighted 2 ms proper acceleration. Material and friction values are estimated.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (1,604 steps); demo: 1.0 (363 steps, 18.15 s). One fixed layout; no robustness claim.
